newsitem.title: FINLAND: Goldman Sachs rates M-Serla outperformer.
newsitem.headline: Goldman Sachs rates M-Serla outperformer.

text.p: Goldman Sachs rated Finnish forestry group Metsa-Serla Oy "market outperformer" and UPM-Kymmene Oy and Enso Oy "market performers" in a report dated on October 30.

"Metsa-Serla offers primarily a very attractive valuation, and the absence of newsprint assets on the balance sheet may help sentiment for these shares in the near to medium term," Goldman Sachs said.
Metsa-Serla's pre-tax profits are expected to turn higher in 1997 after a slump this year, but UPM's and Enso's profits are expected to fall through 1996 and 1997, it said.
Goldman Sachs sees Metsa-Serla's adjusted earnings per share at 0.70 markka in 1996, at 3.20 markka in 1997 and at 6.80 markka in 1998 after 8.1 of 1995.

UPM's EPS is expected to be 11.10 markka in 1996, 10.30 markka in 1997 and 17.6 markka in 1998 after 20.10 markka of 1995, and Enso's EPS is expected to be 4.70 markka in 1996, 4.3 markka in 1997 and 7.2 markka in 1998 after 10.7 markka in 1995.
Goldman Sachs said it had gradually reduced its sector weighting and downgraded all its key buy recommendations for forestries.

"As previously indicated, our new EPS estimates represent significant downward adjustments; 1996 earnings have been cut by 10-15 percent and 1997 earnings by 20-50 percent; we also introduce earnings estimates for 1998 representing a substantial improvement on what we expect to be a disappointing 1997," it said in its analysis covering Finnish, Swedish and Norwegian forestries.
The fundamentals do not yet support a sustainable upswing in the forest industry, it said.
"We continue to advise a market weighting of the sector, with a negative bias," Goldman Sachs said.
